title: Ike on near-identical songs by coincidence
summary: Ike Robinson recalls a friend's song that turned up on a record almost note for note, and Levy calls it coincidence.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, this, this boy that I used to work with, this Italian boy, he wrote a song and he asked me to, in fact, you took it down. Uh-huh. And, uh, it was real fine. And, uh, I was playing some records over one day at my house and I ran into Perry Coleman and he sang the same number, just a different title, different record. It was so close together you couldn't tell. Yeah. We never had heard it.
A coincidence. A coincidence. Just a thousand of miles away and direct coincidence like that.

I took it back and took the record over and he heard it and he said, well, can you imagine this? Oh. A song that come to him. Mm-hmm. So, who else was writing in the, in the period you started? Do you remember any of the fellas around town? Uh.
